title: Jeremiah Stands Trial
description: At the beginning of King Jehoiakim's reign, the Lord commanded Jeremiah to stand in the courtyard of the temple and proclaim that if the people did not repent, the house of the Lord would become like Shiloh, and Jerusalem a curse. The priests, prophets, and people seized him and demanded his death. When Judah's leaders came from the king's house, Jeremiah defended himself by saying the Lord had sent him, and warned against shedding innocent blood. The leaders and the people acquitted him, and the elders of the land recalled how the prophet Micah of Moreshet prophesied similarly in the days of King Hezekiah without being put to death. In contrast, it is told about Uriah the prophet, son of Shemaiah from Kiriath-Jearim, who was brought back from Egypt and killed by King Jehoiakim. Finally, Ahikam, son of Shaphan, protected Jeremiah from being handed over to the people.
